speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your consultation. I need to examine the skin lesion you are concerned about; could you please describe its appearance, including its size, color, and any changes you've noticed recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history; the combination of a non-healing penile lesion and a finger lesion in a 62-year-old male smoker raises concern for squamous cell carcinoma. Have these lesions changed in size, become painful, or started bleeding recently?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Non-healing, crusty, red lesions on the penile shaft and left middle finger. I also have Lesions are painless, History of unsuccessful treatment for syphilis and eczema. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Pneumonia and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That mention of "Pneumonia" seems incorrect for these specific skin lesions; could you clarify if you have any respiratory symptoms like cough or shortness of breath, or if this was a misunderstanding? Also, have you noticed these lesions ulcerating, bleeding, or growing rapidly in the last few weeks?

REQUEST IMAGES: [Penile lesion, Left middle finger lesion]

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No known malignancies or hereditary diseases in the family. Previous treatments for syphilis and eczema. Social history: Lives with his 4th wife, smokes 2 packs of cigarettes per day for the last 30 years, has recently immigrated from Africa.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the history; the heavy smoking history and non-healing nature of these lesions are highly concerning. Could you confirm if the finger lesion is on a sun-exposed area like the dorsal side, and do you have a history of chronic genital ulceration or genital warts?

REQUEST IMAGES: [Penile lesion, Left middle finger lesion]

speaker: Patient
text: Denies any systemic symptoms such as fever, weight loss, night sweats, or malaise. No other similar lesions elsewhere on the body.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Penis and Finger (likely arising from chronic genital ulceration/syphilis on the penis and chronic hand trauma on the finger), supported by the patient's significant smoking history and the non-healing, crusty nature of the lesions.
